description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:980-994 (MemoryBackend::is_contact_blocked).

The implementation queries inner.objects_ref("ChatContact", account_id) for contact_id. Per draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §ChatContact (line 367-370), ChatContact.id is 'the userId provided by the authentication layer: it is the single, global identity key for that user within this deployment.'

So 'is contact X blocked by account A?' is well-defined: look up ChatContact with id=X in account A's contact list. The implementation does this. OK.

But the trait method signature (backend.rs:598-605) takes account_id AND contact_id, and the doc comment on the trait method says 'when the requesting account corresponds to a ChatContact whose blocked is true on the recipient's contact list, the server MUST silently suppress'. The handler at chat.rs:617-620 calls is_contact_blocked(caller, &account_id, contact_id) where contact_id is the chat's contact_id (the OTHER party in a direct chat).

Reading sequence (handler perspective): account_id is the SENDER's account; contact_id is the RECIPIENT (who might have blocked the sender). But MemoryBackend reads from account_id's ChatContact store — i.e. it's checking 'is the recipient blocked by the sender' (the wrong direction).

Spec intent (commit d68b4e3 per the trait doc): suppress the event for the RECIPIENT if the recipient has blocked the sender. The reference impl checks the wrong direction.

Trigger condition: a sender attempts to send a typing indicator to a recipient who has blocked them. Spec says: silently suppress. Current code: returns whether the SENDER has blocked the RECIPIENT (a different question).

This is reachable but its impact is bounded because the kit doesn't gate fan-out on the result — it 'observes' it (chat.rs:617-620 has  and discards). So today the wrong-direction check has zero effect. But when a future consumer wires the predicate into transport fan-out, the bug surfaces.

Fix: the trait signature needs to be clearer about whose perspective. Either:
- rename: is_blocked_by(blocker_principal, blockee_principal) — explicit direction.
- OR: keep the name but document that the predicate is invoked from the RECIPIENT's transport, with account_id == recipient's account, contact_id == sender's ChatContact.id.

The current naming is ambiguous and the reference impl reads the wrong direction.
title: MemoryBackend.is_contact_blocked uses get_objects(account_id) but ChatContact.id is global identity; cross-account scoping unclear
